Wrapping Cloudflare workers and third-party API endpoints with Kong's key authentication

This demo aims to:

- Enable `api.raunaqgupta.com`
- Expose various single-function cloudflare workers under the `/utilities` path.
- Expose my aqicn.org API token protected endpoint under the `/aqi` path without exposing the token.
- Enable key authentication on all endpoints via Kong Konnect.
- Expose a basic single-response AI endpoint under the `/ai` path.

## Enable the `api` sub-domain

- Kong Konnect's free tier provides one free API gateway.
- Provisioned API gateway can be configured for a non-apex domain.

## Expose a datetime utility under `/utilities`

- Created a Cloudflare worker to return the current date and time in JSON format with an optional `timezone` query parameter.
- Setup route on Kong Konnect's API gateway to redirect to `/utilities/datetime`.

curl -X GET "https://api.raunaqgupta.com/utilities/datetime?timezone=PST"

## Expose an air quality index endpoint under `/aqi`

## STAR methodology

S – Situation: A description of the circumstance leading up to the skill being demonstrated. Don’t give too many details, just enough so that the interviewer understands the scenario.
T – Task: What were you doing and what was the goal?
A – Action: What you did specifically to achieve that goal. There is no ‘we’ in this section, just ‘I’.
R – Result: What was the outcome as a result of your performance? Try to include figures and statistics if you have them.

## Most Commonly Asked Behavioral Questions

Q. What was the most difficult decision you had to make?

Situation

The product manager was changing countries in the middle of our alpha preview of Database monitoring. We had meetings lined up with 8 Splunk O11y Cloud customers and he couldn't be available for the first 1 month.

Task

I had to coordinate with the engineering manager, the documentation writer, and our product marketing manager on who will be driving these meetings.

Action

Since I was closest to product from an end-to-end perspective, I ended up taking charge of meetings for the first half of the alpha preview. I wrote a script on how these recurring meetings would be handled to ensure these customers felt heard and were able to see the full advantage of the new feature that we were in the process of releasing. I had help from engineering manager for tasks which required technical finesse specifically around configuring our telemetry pipelines in the backend.

Result

We had a successful 2 month alpha preview which consisted of weekly recurring meetings with 8 Splunk O11y Cloud customers spanning a total of close to 60 hours.

Q. What are your greatest strengths? Weaknesses?

My greatest strength is being obsessed with technical details. I believe good developer experiences can only be designed by being well versed with the quirks of the technology keeping in line with the philosophy of bauhaus principles.

My greatest weakness is sometimes getting too caught up in technical details, which can slow down decision-making. I'm actively working on balancing attention to detail with efficiency.

Q. What was the most significant thing you accomplished in your most recent job?

Launching the database monitoring extension on Splunk O11y Cloud. This happened right after the Splunk acquisition. I had to learn a new product, a new design system, coordinate with a new design team, as well as build relationships with a brand new workstream. On top of that, database monitoring was the first extension built on top of Splunk O11y Cloud after the acquistion. All prior extensions were Splunk's own acquisitions.

Q. Why should we hire you?

I'm deeply interested in the developer tooling space. I have both an engineering and design background which specifically targets this market. I also have prior experience working at both early stage startups as well as large enterprises, which gives me a unique perspective on how to build products fast as well for scale.

Q. What are your salary requirements?

I'm looking for base cash compensation of $260k annually with a target total compensation of $400k annually. However, I'm open to discussing the full compensation package including equity, bonuses, and benefits.

A. I came up with the concept of composite components in Figma which urges all Figma artifacts to be comprised of nothing but components of various complexities. This also uses a noun-verb approach to define jobs which are then strung together to form workflows. This was presented to the entire design team last year and has seen a slow but favorable adoption.

For the better part of my tenure at PlanetScale, I was working out of India while PlanetScale's primary team was based out of Mountain View and slowly growing all over the world. Here are some work ethics I learned and grew to respect, and cherish during my time there.

## Points for consideration

### Give everything a 24-hour window to resolve

This enables people in other time zones to contribute to the discussion. This obviously cannot always be adhered (e.g. certain fixes or updates are merely rubber stamps and do not concern everyone).

### Reduce synchronous online meetings

Not everyone is capable of joining meetings late into the night. These meetings also lead to knowledge not being written down for other team members to read and provide feedback on.

### Create extensive paper trails

Defocusing online meetings in favor of written communication leads to better comments and more context for everyone trying to understand and catch up on decisions being made post-facto.

### Prioritize lengthier feedback over constant back and forth

Discussing and asking questions on Github issues and pull requests and other documents (e.g. Google Docs) provides the ability to see a project/feature as a whole, in-time collation of decisions that are being made and keeps the entire team in the loop.

### Don't summon people on realtime communication platforms

I feel most people have an implicitly understanding of this but mentioning someone on slack beyond regular work hours will not lead to a faster resolution. At the same time, asking someone to resolve something on Slack is bound to get lost and is detrimental to points raised before.

## Conclusion

These strategies have enabled me to counter fatigue, misdirection, loss of information, and enabling everyone in the team to feel connected and responsible towards the product.

## Problem definition

Cisco's upcoming observability platform (aptly called Cisco Observability Platform) wanted to bolster its narrative of full-stack observability to incorporate security monitoring amongst the usual suspects of application performance monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, and digital experience monitorinng.

This would also be the first step towards a stronger narrative between Cisco's security and observability initiatives. The narrative link will also eventually help in cross-sells.

## My role

I was the lead designer within the core team (1 product manager, 5 engineers, 1 user researcher). I drove:

1. Visioning and refinement of the core use cases.
2. Designing the information architecutre of the application.
3. Migration of the entire application to a new design system.
4. Helped define behavior of the extension/module system within the platform.

## Exploring the feasible landscape

We had a good sense of the problem space, with some features such as vulnerability detection being highly feasible. Data security on the other hand was a new area for both the product and engineering team. Multiple rounds of wireframes, and high-fidelity prototypes were utilized to initiate conversations with security engineers and leaders within Cisco to understand the likelihood of adoption, and profitability of building such a thing.

## v0: Building a demo

The very first version of the web application was purely to demo the core APIs being developed in tandem. The UI let a user create an account, create a company, add users to the company, create database clusters, and create keyspaces within those clusters. Amongst a garish orange backdrop.

<Gallery collection={frontmatter.v0}/>

## How does one sell sharding?

Sharding lets you split your database into smaller, more manageable pieces, called shards. Each shard can be hosted on a different server, allowing for better performance and scalability. This was the core value proposition of PlanetScale, but it was also a complex concept to grasp for new users.

Design outcomes were focused on making sharding more approachable, and selling its benefits without overwhelming users with technical jargon.

### Improving dashboards

The database's sharding configuration was visually made more striking to make it easier to understand the databases' current setup at a glance.

<FlexColumn>
  ![Before](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbaas-planetscale/v1-database.png?f=avif)
  ![After](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbaas-planetscale/v2-database.png?f=avif)
</FlexColumn>

### Resharding: From complex config files to simplifying decisions

For a user to reconfigure their database's sharding setup, they would have to modify and update the sharding scheme, and redeploy the database. We first introduced versioning for users to keep track of the changes that were made to the sharding scheme over time.

It was becoming clear that power users could deal with configuration files without using the UI, and to sell sharding we needed to simplify it further. To that end, we removed the need for users to define a sharding scheme altogether and instead, let them focus on the end goal of increasing the number of shards.

<FlexColumn>
  ![Sharding scheme](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbaas-planetscale/v1-resharding.png?f=avif)
  ![With version history](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbaas-planetscale/v2-resharding.png?f=avif)
  ![Simplifying decisions](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbaas-planetscale/v3-resharding.png?f=avif)
</FlexColumn>

## Bring your own database

One of the engineers realized that to showcase the power of PlanetScale's sharding technology, we could let users bring their own existing MySQL databases and shard them on PlanetScale's infrastructure. This would allow users to see the benefits of sharding without having to set up a new database from scratch.

My job then was to help design the user flows and UI components to make this process as seamless as possible. We called this feature internally: "Bring Your Own Database" (BYOD).

## Problem definition: Defining the gap

Splunk Observability Cloud excelled at application and infrastructure monitoring but lacked the end-to-end insight that database monitoring would provide. That gap forced users to switch tools, even as public forum requests and AppDynamics' $50M ARR success showed clear demand. Launching database monitoring would close the application-database performance divide and unlock new personas like database administrators, thereby expanding Splunk Observability Cloud's total addressable market.

![Before Database monitoring](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/case-study/defining-the-gap-before.png?f=avif)

![After Database monitoring](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/case-study/defining-the-gap-after.png?f=avif)

![The Splunk Ideas community helps prioritize feature requests on the roadmap](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/case-study/existing-feedback.png?f=avif)

![Database monitoring is a crucial block in all compelling observability platforms](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/case-study/competitive-analysis.png?f=avif)

## My role

As lead designer for the core team (1 product manager, 12 engineers), I drove the design vision for Database Monitoring. I collaborated cross-functionally with the APM team's lead designer and product manager to integrate workflows between Database Monitoring and Application Performance Monitoring. Additionally, I partnered with the AI engineering team to design and prioritize intelligent features, including query summarization and AI-powered recommendations.

![Project timeline](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/case-study/project-timeline.png?f=avif)

## Impact

Alpha launch of Database monitoring had 11 multinational enterprise customers with a conversion rate upwards of 60% within 3 months of launch in November of 2025. The number of annual licenses is currently targeted at 25 by the end of Q1 2026.

> "Our database team use SolarWinds. dbmon [sic database monitoring] gives me query plan information that I'll only know once the application developer knows the issue is with the database... and when the database team will be looped in eventually to the ticket."

## Designing an MVP

The first launch targeted query analytics, enabling workflows joining APM and Database monitoring, as well as providing AI-assisted summarization, and recommendation capabilities. The MVP focused on three core user needs:

1. Surface vital metrics and visualize query explain plans for database queries,
2. Correlate database queries with application traces, and
3. Launch database monitoring with AI-assisted workflows.

Along the way, I ended up:

1. Defining a new design pattern (In-context previews), and
2. Experimenting with in-product marketing to encourage product-led adoption

## Key design decisions

Following are notable design decisions I made as part of the database monitoring initiative.

### In-context preview

The in-context preview utilizes the concept of [transclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transclusion) to provide a non-disruptive way to access detailed information without navigating away from the current context. This was especially important when users were investigating application traces and needed to quickly understand the associated database queries.
![Location agnostic in-context object preview](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/case-study/in-context-preview.png?f=avif)

### The query execution plan visualization

The query execution plan was visualized using a tree structure to represent the various operations involved in executing a database query. Micro-interactions were obsessed over to ensure that the tree structure was intuitive and easy to navigate. This is now part of the Splunk UI's design system.

![Query execution plan visualization](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/case-study/query-execution-plan.png?f=avif)

### AI-assisted workflows

I defined and designed AI-assisted workflows such as query summarization, and AI-based recommendations to help users optimize their database queries. These features were prioritized based on competitive analysis, and engineering complexity. These are currently in customer preview and are getting positive feedback.

#### A. On demand AI-generated query summarization

Query summarization is a quick-win, highly deterministic AI-assisted solution to the problem of, “What is this SQL query trying to do?” A question that gets asked very often by SREs who are not the developers who wrote the query in the first place. This helps them figure out everything from the importance of said query, troubleshooting  the query, to contacting the appropriate application team if all else fails.

<Gallery collection={frontmatter.aiQuerySummarization}/>

#### B. AI recommendations for query optimization

AI recommendations was an obvious next step to utilize AI to help users optimize their slow-running database queries. The design took into consideration that there were engineering constraints which prevented ahead-of-time AI analysis of ingested queries. Hence, the design focused on an on-demand system where users could request AI recommendations for specific queries they were investigating.

<Gallery collection={frontmatter.aiQueryRecommendation}/>


### In-product marketing to enable product-led adoption

This additional initiative targeted the opportunity to educate users about database monitoring within the product itself. Instead of relying on the stark zero state that Splunk Observability Cloud was using for existing verticals, I designed an in-product marketing experience that would educate users about the value proposition of database monitoring, and encourage them to contact the sales team to enable the feature.

## Targeting the hobby developer market

Hobby developers are not paying enterprise customers. But they can eventually be in the future. This was the bet on which PlanetScale decided to rebrand itself in late 2020, targeting indie developers and hobbyists.

Part of that effort was to reimagine the login and onboarding workflow for PlanetScale's dashboard. The goal was to remove as much friction as possible for a hobby developer to get started with a free PlanetScale database, while leaning into the brand's minimalist, and edgy aesthetic.

This was a hugely successful effort and part of the initiative to rebrand PlanetScale, targeting indie developers, which ultimately led to a [$50M Series C round led by Kleiner Perkins](https://techcrunch.com/2021/11/16/planetscale-raises-50m-series-c-as-its-enterprise-database-service-hits-general-availability/) in November of 2021.
